translations.literal: The emperor blamed Shiyao for dawdling and cowardice, stripped his office, but ordered him to remain with the army managing supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor censured Shiyao for dilatoriness and timidity, dismissed him, but kept him with the army supervising grain transport.

sentences.zh: 侍堯旋督兵赴伏羌。

translations.literal: Shiyao soon led troops to Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyao then marched troops to Fuxiang.

sentences.zh: 福康安至軍，發侍堯玩愒貽誤諸罪狀。

translations.literal: When Fukang'an reached the army he reported Shiyao's dallying, negligence, and other offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an arrived at the front and impeached Shiyao for slackness and dereliction.

sentences.zh: 逮熱河行在，王大臣按鞫，擬斬決。

translations.literal: He was arrested and taken to the imperial residence at Rehe; princes and ministers investigated and proposed immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought to the emperor at Rehe, tried by princes and senior officials, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 上仍令從寬改監候。

translations.literal: The emperor still ordered leniency, changing the sentence to deferred execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again showed mercy, commuting the sentence to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 五十年，諭釋之。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year an edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 50 he was pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 署正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: He served as acting Commandant of the Han Military Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting commandant of the Han Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 湖北江陵民訴知縣孔毓檀侵賑，命侍堯往按。

translations.literal: People of Jiangling in Hubei accused Magistrate Kong Yutan of embezzling relief funds; Shiyao was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling commoners accused Magistrate Kong Yutan of diverting relief grain, Shiyao was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 奏言毓檀未侵賑，但治賑遲緩，坐奪官。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Yutan had not embezzled relief but had been dilatory in relief administration, and Yutan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He found no embezzlement but faulted Yutan's slow relief work and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 命署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Governor-General of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 奏上年孝感被災饑民劉金立等掠穀，生員梅調元糾眾毆殺金立，並生瘞二十三人。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the previous year famine victims of Xiaogan including Liu Jinli had plundered grain; licentiate Mei Tiaoyuan rallied a crowd, beat Jinli to death, and had twenty-three people buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that during last year's famine in Xiaogan, Liu Jinli and other starving villagers had looted grain; licentiate Mei Tiaoyuan rallied a mob that beat Jinli to death and buried twenty-three people alive.

sentences.zh: 上逮前總督特成額及知縣秦樸等治其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the former Governor-General Te Cheng'e, Magistrate Qin Pu, and others arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had former Governor-General Te Cheng'e, Magistrate Qin Pu, and others arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，實授。

translations.literal: Before long, he received actual appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, he was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, he went to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year, he went to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 台灣民林爽文為亂，調侍堯閩浙總督，駐蚶江。

translations.literal: Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen raised rebellion; Shiyao was transferred as Governor-General of Min-Zhe and stationed at Hanzhen River.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Shiyao was transferred to Governor-General of Fujian-Zhejiang and posted at Hanzhen River.

sentences.zh: 時前總督常青督兵渡台灣，侍堯以兵力不足，調廣東、浙江兵濟師。

translations.literal: At the time former Governor-General Changqing supervised troops crossing to Taiwan; Shiyao because troops were insufficient, transferred Guangdong and Zhejiang soldiers to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor-General Changqing was then leading troops across to Taiwan; finding the force insufficient, Shiyao drew reinforcements from Guangdong and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 又慮賊據笨港劫糧械，撥繪船分防鹿耳門、鹿仔港。

translations.literal: Also fearing bandits occupying Bengang to plunder grain and weapons, he deployed painted boats to divide defense of Lu'ermen and Luzai Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing rebels might seize Bengang and raid supplies, he deployed patrol boats to guard Lu'ermen and Luzai Harbor.

sentences.zh: 上獎以籌濟有方。

translations.literal: The emperor rewarded him for planning relief with method.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his well-organized provisioning.

sentences.zh: 亂久未定，上以常青非將才，命福康安為將軍督師；

translations.literal: The rebellion long unsettled, the emperor because Changqing was not general talent, ordered Fuk'anggan as general to supervise the army;
translations.idiomatic: As the rebellion dragged on, the emperor judged Changqing no commander and sent Fuk'anggan as general to take charge;

sentences.zh: 並寄諭常青全師以歸，待福康安至，再籌進取。

translations.literal: And sent sealed instruction to Changqing to bring the whole army back, wait until Fuk'anggan arrived, then again plan advance.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Changqing in a sealed message to withdraw the entire force and await Fuk'anggan's arrival before planning further operations.

sentences.zh: 侍堯恐常青宣露上旨，人心惶惑，節錄發寄，並具疏請罪。

translations.literal: Shiyao feared Changqing would reveal the emperor's intent and people's hearts would be alarmed and confused, excerpted and sent the message, and also submitted a memorial asking punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyao feared that revealing the imperial directive would unsettle the troops; he therefore sent only an excerpt and submitted a memorial asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，獎以「深合機宜，得大臣體」。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly pleased, rewarded him with "Deeply fitting opportunity, obtaining a grand minister's manner."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and praised him: "Deeply appropriate to the moment—true ministerial conduct."

sentences.zh: 賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Granted double-eyed peacock plume.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 福康安劾提督柴大紀，上責侍堯徇隱。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan impeached Regional Commander Chai Daji; the emperor blamed Shiyao for favoring concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan impeached Regional Commander Chai Daji, and the emperor faulted Shiyao for shielding him.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，侍堯亦奏大紀貪劣諸狀，自請治罪，上寬之。

translations.literal: Fifty-third year, Shiyao also memorialized Chai Daji's greedy bad aspects, himself asked punishment, the emperor was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year Shiyao too memorialized Chai Daji's corruption and asked that he himself be punished; the emperor showed lenience.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，命仍襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Taiwan pacified, ordered still to inherit earldom.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan was pacified, he was allowed to retain his earldom.

sentences.zh: 建福康安等生祠於台灣，命侍堯居福康安、海蘭察之次。

translations.literal: Built life temples to Fuk'anggan and others in Taiwan, ordered Shiyao to rank after Fuk'anggan and Hailancha.
translations.idiomatic: Life temples to Fuk'anggan and others were built in Taiwan, with Shiyao ranked next after Fuk'anggan and Hailancha.

sentences.zh: 復命圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣。

translations.literal: Again ordered portrait in Hall of Purple Splendor, listed among the first twenty meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered depicted in the Hall of Purple Splendor among the twenty foremost contributors.

sentences.zh: 侍堯短小精敏，過目成誦。

translations.literal: Shiyao was short in stature, keen and sharp, read once and could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyao was short but quick-witted, with a memory that retained whatever he read at a glance.

sentences.zh: 見屬僚，數語即辨其才否。

translations.literal: Seeing subordinate officials, a few words and he could distinguish their talent or not.
translations.idiomatic: After a few words with his subordinates, he could tell whether they were capable.

sentences.zh: 擁幾高坐，語所治肥瘠利害，或及其陰事，若親見。

translations.literal: Holding table sitting high, speaking of what he governed fat-thin benefit-harm, or reaching their private affairs, as if seen in person.
translations.idiomatic: Seated at his desk, he would speak of what thrived or languished under each man's administration—and sometimes of their private scandals—as though he had witnessed them himself.

sentences.zh: 人皆悚懼。

translations.literal: People all were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: All were terrified.

sentences.zh: 屢以貪黷坐法，上終憐其才，為之曲赦。

translations.literal: Repeatedly because of corruption violated law, the emperor ultimately pitied his talent, for him bent pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly convicted of graft, the emperor still valued his talent and repeatedly bent the law in his favor.

sentences.zh: 十月，疾聞，命其子侍衛毓秀往省。

translations.literal: Tenth month, illness reported, ordered his son Bodyguard Yu Xiu to go visit.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his illness came in the tenth month, the emperor sent his son, Imperial Bodyguard Yu Xiu, to visit him.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，諡恭毅。

translations.literal: Shortly after died, posthumous title Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was given the posthumous title Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 弟奉堯，自官學生襲勳舊佐領，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: Younger brother Fengyao, from student of the Imperial Academy inherited old merit assistant commandant, appointed Blue Plume Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fengyao inherited an old hereditary assistant commandant's post from the Imperial Academy and was appointed a Blue Plume Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 累遷江南提督。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to Regional Commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Forty-fifth year, inherited earldom.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，調福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: Forty-sixth year, transferred to Fujian land Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to Regional Commander of Fujian infantry.

sentences.zh: 以漳、泉累有械鬥，左授馬蘭鎮總​​兵。

translations.literal: Because Zhang and Quan repeatedly had armed fights, demoted to Malan garrison general.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated armed brawls in Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, he was relegated to commander of the Malan garrison.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，署直隸提督。

translations.literal: Fifty-second year, acting Regional Commander of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he served as acting Regional Commander of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 山東學政劉權之移家，舟經靜海被盜，下吏議。

translations.literal: Shandong Education Commissioner Liu Quanzhi moved house, boat passing Jinghai was robbed, handed to officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong Education Commissioner Liu Quanzhi moved his household, his boat was robbed in Jinghai and the case was sent for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 上以署事未久，且隨扈熱河，寬之。

translations.literal: The emperor because acting office not long, and moreover accompanied entourage to Rehe, was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed lenience, noting that Fengyao had held the acting post only briefly and was then accompanying the court at Rehe.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，侍堯還襲伯爵，加奉堯提督銜。

translations.literal: Fifty-third year, Shiyao again inherited earldom, added Fengyao Regional Commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year Shiyao resumed the earldom and Fengyao was granted the rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒，諡慎簡。

translations.literal: Fifty-fourth year, died, posthumous title Shengjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-fourth year and was given the posthumous title Shengjian.

sentences.zh: 子毓文，乾隆六十年，侍堯督雲、貴與局員通同偷減錢法事發，奪毓秀伯爵，命毓文承襲。

translations.literal: Son Yuwen; Qianlong sixtieth year, Shiyao supervising Yunnan-Guizhou with board member conspiring secretly reduce coinage law affair exposed, stripped Yu Xiu's earldom, ordered Yuwen to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuwen: in the sixtieth year of Qianlong, when the scandal of Shiyao's collusion with mint officials in Yunnan-Guizhou to secretly reduce coin standards came to light, Yu Xiu's earldom was revoked and Yuwen was ordered to inherit.

sentences.zh: =伍彌泰=伍彌泰，伍彌氏，蒙古正黃旗人，副將軍三等伯阿喇納子。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai, of the Wu Mi clan, a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner, son of Deputy General third-class count Alana.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mitai was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner, of the Wu Mi clan, and the son of Deputy General and third-class count Alana.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰以雍正二年襲爵。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai in Yongzheng second year inherited title.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mitai inherited his title in the second year of Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 授公中佐領，擢散秩大臣，遷鑲白旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: Appointed company commander in public service, promoted to minister without portfolio, transferred to Bordered White Banner Mongol vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a company commander, promoted to minister without portfolio, and transferred to vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Mongol Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十五年，賜伯號曰誠毅。

translations.literal: Qianlong fifteenth year, granted count title name Chengyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Qianlong he was granted the count's style name Chengyi ("Sincere and Resolute").

sentences.zh: 二十年，授涼州將軍。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, appointed Liangzhou General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed General of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 旋命以將軍銜駐西藏辦事，二十四年，代還，授正藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Shortly ordered with general rank stationed in Tibet for affairs, twenty-fourth year replaced and returned, appointed Plain Blue Banner Mongol commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Tibet as resident commissioner with the rank of general; returning in the twenty-fourth year, he was made commander-in-chief of the Plain Blue Mongol Banner.

sentences.zh: 出為江寧將軍。

translations.literal: Went out as Jiangning General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上以伍彌泰不勝任，召還，仍為散秩大臣。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, the emperor because Wu Mitai not up to the task, summoned back, still served as minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the emperor judged Wu Mitai unequal to the post and recalled him, retaining him as a minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 命協辦伊犁事務。

translations.literal: Ordered to assist Ili affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to assist in Ili affairs.

sentences.zh: 哈薩克越境游牧，師逐之出塞。

translations.literal: Kazakhs crossed border to pasture, army drove them out of the frontier pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Kazakhs crossed the border to graze, troops drove them beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上以伍彌泰不諳軍務，令隨行學習。

translations.literal: The emperor because Wu Mitai not versed in military affairs, ordered him to accompany and learn.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Wu Mitai unversed in military affairs, the emperor had him accompany the campaign to learn.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命往烏魯木齊辦事。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, ordered to go to Urumchi for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was sent to Urumchi as resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 築精河屯堡，上賜名曰綏來。

translations.literal: Built Jinghe fortified colony, the emperor granted name called Suilai.
translations.idiomatic: He built a fortified settlement at Jinghe, which the emperor named Suilai.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，代還，署鑲黃蒙古、正白漢軍兩旗都統。

translations.literal: Thirty-first year, replaced and returned, acting Bordered Yellow Mongol and Plain White Han Chinese Banner commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in the thirty-first year, he served concurrently as acting commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Mongol and Plain White Han Chinese Banners.

sentences.zh: 授內大臣。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Grand Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，命往西寧辦事。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year, ordered to go to Xining for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he was sent to Xining as resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 郭羅剋土番劫洞庫爾種人行李，伍彌泰遣兵逐捕，得行李以還。

translations.literal: Guoluo Tibetan bandits robbed Dongkur people's luggage, Wu Mitai sent troops to pursue and capture, obtained luggage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoluo Tibetans robbed the Dongkur tribesmen's baggage, Wu Mitai sent troops in pursuit and recovered the goods.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，上以未痛剿，責伍彌泰怠忽。

translations.literal: Reported to the throne, the emperor because not thoroughly suppressed, blamed Wu Mitai for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported this, the emperor faulted him for not crushing the raiders thoroughly, charging negligence.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，改駐西藏辦事。

translations.literal: Thirty-eighth year, changed to stationed in Tibet for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was reassigned as resident commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，代還，擢理籓院尚書，兼鑲白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: Forty-first year, replaced and returned, promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, concurrently Bordered White Banner Han Chinese commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in the forty-first year, he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and made concurrent commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Han Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 出為綏遠城將軍，調西安。

translations.literal: Went out as Suiyuan city General, transferred to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Suiyuan and then transferred to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，伊犁將軍伊勒圖請以屯田無眷屬之兵次第撤回，下伍彌泰議。

translations.literal: Forty-third year, Ili General Yiletui requested to gradually withdraw garrison-farming soldiers without dependents, handed down to Wu Mitai for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year General Yiletui of Ili proposed gradually withdrawing garrison-farming troops without families; the matter was referred to Wu Mitai.

sentences.zh: 選陝、甘綠營兵三千攜眷屬以往。

translations.literal: Selected Shaanxi-Gansu Green Standard soldiers three thousand carrying dependents to go.
translations.idiomatic: He selected three thousand Green Standard troops from Shaanxi and Gansu, with their families, to go.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，班禪額爾德尼詣京師，命伍彌泰護行，仍還西安。

translations.literal: Forty-fifth year, Panchen Erdeni came to capital, ordered Wu Mitai to escort, still returned to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year, when the Panchen Lama came to the capital, Wu Mitai was ordered to escort him and then return to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，撒拉爾回蘇四十三等為亂，陷河州。

translations.literal: Forty-sixth year, Salar Muslims Su Forty-three and others made rebellion, captured Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year Salar Muslims led by Su Forty-three rebelled and seized Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 上命伍彌泰選兵千人備徵發。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wu Mitai to select soldiers one thousand to prepare for mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wu Mitai to ready a thousand troops for deployment.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰奏提督馬彪已率兵赴河州，擬選滿洲兵千繼往。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai memorialized Regional Commander Ma Biao already led troops to Hezhou, planned to select Manchu soldiers one thousand to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mitai reported that Regional Commander Ma Biao had already marched on Hezhou and proposed sending a thousand Manchu troops after him.

sentences.zh: 上以所奏與諭旨合，深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor because what was memorialized accorded with edict, deeply praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was much pleased that the proposal matched his own instructions.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士阿桂視師，督軍攻華林山梁，命伍彌泰駐龍尾山為聲援。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to inspect the army, supervise troops to attack Hualin mountain ridge, ordered Wu Mitai stationed at Longwei mountain as sound support.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui was sent to direct operations against Hualin Ridge, while Wu Mitai was posted on Longwei Mountain as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 回亂旋定，捕得阿渾五。

translations.literal: Hui rebellion shortly pacified, captured Ahunwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Muslim rebellion was soon suppressed and Ahunwu was captured.

sentences.zh: 有海潮宗者，嘗出降，彪遣往開諭，遂留從亂。

translations.literal: There was Haichao Zong, once came out to surrender, Biao sent him to go persuade, then remained following rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: One Haichao Zong had once surrendered; Ma Biao sent him to win others over, but he stayed with the rebels instead.

sentences.zh: 上責伍彌泰等不先奏聞，下吏議奪官，上寬之。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Wu Mitai and others for not first reporting to throne, handed to officials deliberating stripping office, the emperor was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor faulted Wu Mitai and others for not reporting this earlier; dismissal was proposed, but the emperor showed lenience.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，授吏部尚書、協辦大學士、鑲白旗蒙古都統，充上書房總諳達。

translations.literal: Forty-eighth year, appointed Minister of Personnel, Assistant Grand Secretary, Bordered White Banner Mongol commander-in-chief, filled as head instructor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel, Assistant Grand Secretary, and commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Mongol Banner, and served as head Mongol-language instructor in the Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上巡江、浙，命留京辦事，授東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Forty-ninth year, the emperor toured Jiang-Zhe, ordered to remain in capital for affairs, appointed Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured Jiangsu and Zhejiang in the forty-ninth year, Wu Mitai was left in charge at the capital and made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 上以伍彌泰年逾七十，命與大學士嵇璜、蔡新俱日出後入朝，風雪沍寒，免其入直。

translations.literal: The emperor because Wu Mitai age exceeded seventy, ordered with Grand Secretaries Ji Huang and Cai Xin all after sunrise to enter court, wind snow severe cold, exempted their entering duty.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu Mitai was over seventy, he and Grand Secretaries Ji Huang and Cai Xin were permitted to arrive after sunrise; in bitter winter weather they were excused from regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 五十年，預千叟宴。

translations.literal: Fiftieth year, attended Thousand Elderly Feast.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he attended the Feast of a Thousand Elders.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒，贈太子太保，賜祭葬，諡文端。

translations.literal: Fifty-first year, died, posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted sacrificial burial, posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-first year, was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰治事知大體。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai in governing affairs knew the great pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mitai handled affairs with a grasp of the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 班禪額爾德尼至京師，王大臣多和南稱弟子。

translations.literal: Panchen Erdeni arrived at capital, princes and grand ministers mostly joined palms calling themselves disciples.
translations.idiomatic: When the Panchen Lama reached the capital, many princes and ministers bowed with palms together and called themselves his disciples.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰護行，與抗禮。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai escorted on the journey, with him treated as equals in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the Panchen, Wu Mitai treated him as an equal in ceremony.

sentences.zh: =官保=官保，烏雅氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Guan Bao, of the Wuya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bao was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, of the Wuya clan.

sentences.zh: 初授刑部筆帖式，擢堂主事。

translations.literal: At first appointed Board of Punishments clerk, promoted to section chief.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Board of Punishments and rose to section chief.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，授江南江寧知府。

translations.literal: Qianlong seventh year, appointed Jiangnan Jiangning prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qianlong he was appointed prefect of Jiangning in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，總督尹繼善奏官保不宜外任，复授刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, Governor-General Yin Jishan memorialized Guan Bao not suitable for external appointment, again appointed Board of Punishments vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Governor-General Yin Jishan reported that Guan Bao was unsuited to provincial office, and he was recalled to the Board of Punishments as vice director.

sentences.zh: 轉郎中，改御史。

translations.literal: Transferred to bureau director, changed to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a bureau director and then a censor.

sentences.zh: 擢刑科給事中，巡視台灣。

translations.literal: Promoted to supervising censor of Punishments Section, toured and inspected Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted supervising censor of the Punishments Section and sent to inspect Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢鑲黃旗漢軍副都統，往西藏辦事。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, promoted to Bordered Yellow Banner Han Chinese vice commander-in-chief, went to Tibet for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Han Chinese Banner and sent to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year, appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十年，調工部。

translations.literal: Thirtieth year, transferred to Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，復往西藏辦事，察知糧務通判吳元澄以庫銀貿易。

translations.literal: Thirty-second year, again went to Tibet for affairs, discovered grain affairs sub-prefect Wu Yuancheng used treasury silver for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Sent again to Tibet in the thirty-second year, he discovered Sub-Prefect Wu Yuancheng trading with government funds.

sentences.zh: 上以官保初至藏即察奏，嘉其急公，讞實，論斬。

translations.literal: The emperor because Guan Bao upon first arriving at Tibet immediately investigated and reported, praised his urgent public service, verified truth, sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Guan Bao's public-mindedness in reporting the case as soon as he arrived in Tibet; the facts were confirmed and Wu was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 歷正紅旗蒙古、滿洲都統，理籓院，刑、禮、戶諸部尚書。

translations.literal: Successively Plain Red Banner Mongol, Manchu commander-in-chief, Court of Colonial Affairs, Punishments, Rites, Revenue various ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Mongol and Manchu Banners, head of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and Minister of Punishments, Rites, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Thirty-fourth year, Assistant Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he became Assistant Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 上幸熱河，命留京辦事。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Rehe, ordered to remain in capital for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Rehe, Guan Bao was left in charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，調吏部。

translations.literal: Thirty-eighth year, transferred to Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以年逾八十乞休，命致仕。

translations.literal: Forty-first year, because age exceeded eighty begged retirement, ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, being over eighty, he asked to retire and was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡文勤。

translations.literal: Died, granted sacrificial burial, posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was granted state funeral honors and the posthumous title Wenqin.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：廷桂嘗言：「事英主有法。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Tinggui once said: "Serving an enlightened sovereign has a method.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Tinggui once observed: "Serving an enlightened sovereign calls for a method.

sentences.zh: 若先有市惠、好名、黨援諸病，上所知，便一事不可行。

translations.literal: If first there are buying favor, loving reputation, faction support various faults, the sovereign knows, then one thing cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: "If you already suffer from buying favor, craving reputation, or building factions—and the emperor knows it—nothing you propose will go forward.

sentences.zh: 」其言深中高宗之隱，被眷遇宜矣。

translations.literal: " His words deeply hit Gaozong's hidden feelings, received favor and treatment as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " His remark struck deep at what the Gaozong Emperor wished unspoken; small wonder he enjoyed such imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 侍堯眷遇尤厚，屢坐贓敗，屢屈法貸之。

translations.literal: Shiyao's favor and treatment especially deep, repeatedly convicted corruption failure, repeatedly bent law to forgive him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyao enjoyed even greater favor, though repeatedly convicted of graft; each time the law was bent to spare him.

sentences.zh: 蓋特憐其才，非以其工進獻也。

translations.literal: Probably specially pitying his talent, not because he was skilled at presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his talent, not any skill at currying favor.

sentences.zh: 阿彌達、廷璋皆以不謹聞，亦未竟其罪。

translations.literal: Amitai, Tingzhang all because of lack of care were known, also did not exhaust their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Amitai and Tingzhang too were noted for carelessness, yet neither was punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 有恭撫江、浙，治海塘，重水利，有惠於民。

translations.literal: Yougong governed Jiang-Zhe, managed sea dikes, emphasized waterworks, had benefit for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong as governor of Jiangsu and Zhejiang repaired sea walls and prioritized water control, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 其被譴尚非有所私，視侍堯輩故當勝。

translations.literal: His being reprimanded still was not having private reasons, compared with Shiyao's kind therefore ought to surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Even when reprimanded, he was not driven by private motives—and so he stands above men like Shiyao.

sentences.zh: 伍彌泰雖未嘗領疆寄，久於邊徼，恩被延登，在當時亦勞臣也，因附著之。

translations.literal: Wu Mitai although never undertook frontier command responsibility, long at border regions, grace extended and promoted, in that time also a toiling minister, therefore appended and recorded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mitai never held full frontier command, yet after long service on the borders he was raised by imperial grace; he too was a worthy servant of his day, and is therefore included here.
